subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Which attribution fields should become a stable status/sessions.usage JSON contract, and how should channel target privacy be represented?
rationale: Current main partially exposes related metadata, but adding cron job id/name and channel target classification creates a stable external API and privacy boundary that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Add optional privacy-preserving fields
options.body: Add stable optional fields such as agentId, sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, channelTargetKind, model, and runtime while omitting or redacting raw target ids by default.

options.title: Expose target ids behind explicit opt-in
options.body: Add the same attribution fields and require a separate flag or privileged API mode before raw channel target ids or hashes appear in JSON output.

options.title: Defer to external adapters
options.body: Keep core status/usage JSON as-is and accept that dashboards must keep joining session, cron, and channel metadata outside OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Add optional privacy-preserving fields
recommendation.body: Add stable optional fields such as agentId, sessionKind, cronJobId/name, channel, channelTargetKind, model, and runtime while omitting or redacting raw target ids by default.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans session metadata, status/usage JSON contracts, and privacy/product direction, all areas with recent history from this owner candidate.
